problems.title: Average of arithmetic-progression endpoints
problems.question: The first n arithmetic-progression terms have mean 10, and the last term is -2. Find the first term.
problems.idea: An arithmetic progression’s mean is the average of its first and last terms.
steps: Thus a1-2=20 and a1=22.

problems.title: Overlap when circles pass through each other’s centres
problems.question: Each of two circles passes through the other’s centre. Their radius is 2√3. Find their common area.
problems.idea: The centre distance equals the common radius, so each half of the lens is a 120-degree circular segment.
formulas: This follows from two 120° sectors minus their two isosceles triangles.
steps: Each intersection point with the two centres forms an equilateral triangle, producing the 120° sector angle.
Here R²=12. Substitute into the lens-area formula: $24(\pi/3-\sqrt3/4)$.
The result is 8π-6√3.

problems.title: Area of a square in a right triangle
problems.question: A square shares the right-angle vertex of a right triangle with legs 3 and 6 cm; its opposite corner lies on the hypotenuse. Find the square’s area.
problems.idea: Place the legs on coordinate axes and substitute the square corner (s,s) into the hypotenuse equation.
steps: The opposite corner satisfies s/3+s/6=1, so s/2=1 and s=2.
The square’s area is 2²=4 cm².

problems.title: Range on a restricted interval
problems.question: Find the range of y=x²-3x-2 for x∈[1,3].
problems.idea: Complete the square for the minimum and compare endpoint values for the maximum.
steps: The vertex x=3/2 lies in the interval, giving minimum -17/4=-4.25.
The endpoint values are f(1)=-4 and f(3)=-2. Since the parabola decreases to its vertex then increases, the maximum is -2.
The function is continuous, so it takes every value between these extremes.

problems.title: A dilation about the origin
problems.question: A dilation with centre at the origin and factor k sends A=(2,3) to B=(2x-1,x). Find k.
problems.idea: A dilation multiplies both coordinates by the same factor.
steps: The image coordinates satisfy 2k=2x-1 and 3k=x.
Substitute x=3k into the first equation: 2k=6k-1.
Thus 4k=1 and k=1/4.

problems.title: Middle term from a seven-term geometric product
problems.question: The product of the first seven terms of a real geometric progression is 128. Find the fourth term.
problems.idea: Symmetric pairs multiply to the square of the middle term.
steps: Pair the first and seventh, second and sixth, and third and fifth terms. Along with b4, their product is b4⁷.
Thus b4⁷=128=2⁷. An odd power is one-to-one over the real numbers, so b4=2.

problems.title: Minimum of a trigonometric quadratic
problems.question: Find the minimum of 2cos²α+3sinα-3 over real α.
problems.idea: Replace cos²α with 1-sin²α and use the bounds on sine.
steps: On -1≤t≤1, both t+1 and 5-2t are nonnegative.
Therefore E+6≥0, or E≥-6.
At t=-1, the first factor vanishes and E=-6. This sine value is attainable.

problems.title: Change in a pie-chart angle
problems.question: A class initially has 10 boys and 8 girls. Two boys join. By how many degrees does the boys’ pie-chart sector increase?
problems.idea: A sector angle is its category fraction times a full turn.
steps: The original angle is (10/18)·360°=200°.
The new angle is (12/20)·360°=216°.
The increase is 216°-200°=16°.

problems.title: Recover four numbers from mean, median and mode
problems.question: Four numbers have mean 2, median 3, and unique mode 4. Find their range.
problems.idea: Order the numbers and use the median to locate the repeated mode.
formulas: For sorted four values w≤x≤y≤z, median=(x+y)/2.
steps: The mode 4 must appear at least twice. It cannot appear three times because the median would then be 4.
The two 4s must be y=z=4; if a 4 occurred among the first two positions, both middle values would be at least 4.
The median condition gives (x+4)/2=3, so x=2.
The sum gives w+2+4+4=8, so w=-2. The range is 4-(-2)=6.

problems.title: A strict absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Solve |3-x|<2x-3.
problems.idea: The right side must be positive; split at x=3 only after applying that condition.
formulas: |3-x|=3-x for x≤3 and x-3 for x≥3.
steps: First require 2x-3>0, so x>1.5.
For 1.5<x≤3, solve 3-x<2x-3, giving x>2.
For x≥3, solve x-3<2x-3, which is true throughout that interval.
Combining gives x>2, excluding 2 because equality occurs there.

problems.title: Circle circumference compared with a sector arc
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in a sector of central angle 60°. Find the ratio of the circle’s circumference to the sector’s arc length.
problems.idea: The circle centre lies on the sector bisector and is twice its radius away from the sector vertex.
formulas: If centre distance is d and small radius r, r=d sin30°=d/2.
Internal tangency to the sector’s circle gives R=d+r.
Circle circumference 2πr; sector arc Rθ with θ=π/3.
steps: From r=d/2, d=2r. Thus R=3r.
The circle circumference is 2πr, while the sector arc is (π/3)(3r)=πr.
The requested ratio is 2πr/(πr)=2.
problems.note: None of the printed choices gives 2. The choice 0.5 would be the reverse ratio, sector arc divided by small-circle circumference.

problems.title: Evaluate a polynomial from its roots
problems.question: A monic quadratic f(x)=x²+(a+1)x+(b-2) has roots 1 and -5. Find f(√3-2).
problems.idea: The roots determine its factorisation. Complete the square before substituting.
steps: The leading coefficient is 1, so no extra scale factor is needed in the root factorisation.

problems.title: Compare roots with a common power
problems.question: Order √2, cuberoot(3), and sixthroot(6) increasingly.
problems.idea: All are positive. Raising to the same positive power preserves their order.
steps: Compare their sixth powers: 6<8<9.
The original positive numbers have the same order.

problems.title: Perpendicular combinations of two unit vectors
problems.question: Unit vectors a,b satisfy (2a+b) perpendicular to (a+2b). Find the cosine between a,b.
problems.idea: Set the dot product of the two combinations to zero.
formulas: For unit vectors, a·a=b·b=1 and a·b=cosθ.
Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: Expand (2a+b)·(a+2b)=2+4cosθ+cosθ+2.
Thus 4+5cosθ=0.
The cosine is -4/5, which is within the valid interval [-1,1].

problems.title: Maximum integer count in a moving interval
problems.question: What is the greatest possible number of integer solutions to x²-(2b+5)x+5b+b²≤0?
problems.idea: Its two roots are always five units apart. Count integers in the resulting closed interval.
steps: The quadratic is nonpositive exactly for b≤x≤b+5.
A closed interval of length 5 can contain at most 6 integers: seven integers would have first-to-last distance at least 6.
For any integer b, the six integers b,b+1,...,b+5 all satisfy the inequality.

problems.title: A continued-fraction inequality with domain restrictions
problems.question: Solve $\cfrac1{1-\cfrac1{2-\cfrac1{3+\cfrac1x}}}<0$.
problems.idea: Simplify from the inside, retaining every input excluded by an intermediate denominator.
steps: The final denominator is (2x+1)/(5x+2), so the whole expression is (5x+2)/(2x+1).
This ratio is negative only between its pole -1/2 and zero -2/5.
Both endpoints are excluded; the other excluded inputs are outside that interval.

problems.title: A constant plus an infinite geometric tail
problems.question: Find 3/4+1/5+1/25+1/125+....
problems.idea: Sum the geometric tail, then add the initial constant.
steps: The tail has first term 1/5 and ratio 1/5, giving (1/5)/(4/5)=1/4.

problems.title: Area below a section through the centroid
problems.question: Triangle ABC has area 90 cm². A line through its centroid parallel to AC meets AB,BC at M,N. Find the area of trapezoid AMNC.
problems.idea: The small triangle BMN has linear scale 2/3, so its area scale is 4/9.
formulas: The centroid divides every median 2:1 from the vertex.
Area scales as the square of a similarity length scale.
steps: Triangles BMN and BAC are similar with scale 2/3.
The upper triangle area is (4/9)·90=40 cm².
The remaining trapezoid area is 90-40=50 cm².

problems.title: Age of a player who leaves a team
problems.question: Eleven football players have mean age 22. One leaves, and the remaining ten have mean age 21. Find the departing player’s age.
problems.idea: Subtract the remaining age total from the original total.
steps: The original age total is 11·22=242.
The remaining total is 10·21=210.
The difference is 32 years.

problems.title: Choose two boys and two girls
problems.question: Four students are selected uniformly from a group of four boys and three girls. What is the probability of exactly two boys and two girls?
problems.idea: Count the favourable subsets and divide by all four-person subsets.
steps: There are choose(7,4)=35 possible four-person subsets.
The favourable choices are choose(4,2)·choose(3,2)=6·3=18.
The probability is 18/35.

problems.title: Incircle and circumcircle of a regular dodecagon
problems.question: The incircle of a regular dodecagon has area Q. Find the area of its circumcircle.
problems.idea: The inradius is the circumradius times cos15°.
formulas: Circle areas scale as squared radii.
steps: The area ratio is R²/r²=1/cos²15°=4/(2+√3).
Multiply this ratio by Q.

problems.title: Cut a square into a regular octagon
problems.question: Cut all four corners off a square of side 4 cm so that the remaining figure is a regular octagon. Find its area.
problems.idea: Each removed corner is an isosceles right triangle. Set the chamfer length equal to the remaining straight side length.
formulas: If corner legs are t, the chamfer is t√2 and the remaining original side is 4-2t.
steps: Regularity requires t√2=4-2t, so t=4/(2+√2)=4-2√2.
The four removed triangles total 2t²=2(24-16√2)=48-32√2.
The octagon area is 16-(48-32√2)=32√2-32, approximately 13.255 cm².
problems.note: The printed choice 32-32√2 is the negative of the correct area. None of the listed options equals the positive value obtained here.

problems.title: Cancel negative powers before substitution
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac{1+ax^{-1}}{a^{-1}x^{-1}}\cdot\frac{a^{-1}-x^{-1}}{a^{-1}x-ax^{-1}}$ for a=5 and x=1+3√2.
problems.idea: Rewrite negative powers as reciprocals, then cancel factors.
steps: The first fraction becomes ((x+a)/x)·ax=a(x+a).
The second becomes [(x-a)/(ax)]/[(x²-a²)/(ax)]=1/(x+a).
The original domain requires a≠0, x≠0, x≠a,-a. The given values meet all these conditions.
The product is a=5.

problems.title: Circumdisk area from an incenter’s position
problems.question: An isosceles triangle’s incenter divides its base altitude into lengths 20 and 12 cm. Find the area of its circumcircle.
problems.idea: The full altitude is 32; the shorter part is the inradius. Use area and semiperimeter to recover the sides.
formulas: For base b, height h and semiperimeter s: r=bh/(2s)<h/2.
For half-base t and equal side l: r=th/(l+t), and l²=t²+h².
steps: Since h=32 and r<h/2=16, the base-to-incenter part must be r=12.
Let half the base be t. Then 12=32t/(l+t), giving l=5t/3.
Pythagoras gives 25t²/9=t²+1024, so t=24 and l=40. The full base is 48.
The circumcircle area is 625π cm².

problems.title: A segment cut by a concentric-circle tangent
problems.question: Concentric circles have radii 3 and 6. A tangent to the smaller circle cuts off a segment from the larger disk. Find the smaller segment’s area.
problems.idea: The tangent line is three units from the common centre, fixing the larger chord’s central angle.
steps: The centre-to-chord distance is 3, so cos(θ/2)=3/6=1/2. Hence θ=120°.
The sector area is (120/360)·36π=12π.
The triangle between the two radii has area (36/2)sin120°=9√3.
Subtract it from the sector.
